arxiv-1704-03917.title: Spin Hall effect emerging from a noncollinear magnetic lattice without spin-orbit coupling
arxiv-1704-03917.creator: Yang Zhang, Jakub Železný, Yan Sun, Jeroen van den Brink, Binghai Yan
arxiv-1704-03917.description: Abstract The spin Hall effect (SHE), which converts a charge current into a transverse spin current, has long been believed to be a phenomenon induced by the spin–orbit coupling. Here, we identify an alternative mechanism to realize the intrinsic SHE through a noncollinear magnetic structure that breaks the spin rotation symmetry.

arxiv-2105-05306.title: Intelligent interactive technologies for mental health and well-being This a pre-print version of the paper published in: E. Pap (ed.), Artificial Intelligence: Theory and Applications, Studies in Computational Intelligence 973, Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2021, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3
arxiv-2105-05306.creator: Mladjan Jovanovic, Aleksandar Jevremovic, Milica Pejovic-Milovancevic
arxiv-2105-05306.description: Abstract Mental healthcare has seen numerous benefits from interactive technologies and artificial intelligence. Various interventions have successfully used intelligent technologies to automate the assessment and evaluation of psychological treatments and mental well-being and functioning. These technologies include different types of robots, video games, and conversational agents. The paper critically analyzes existing solutions with the outlooks for their future.

arxiv-2105-13958.title: Effects of the Nuclear Equation of State on Type I X-Ray Bursts: Interpretation of the X-Ray Bursts from GS 1826-24 Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2105-13958.creator: A. Dohi (土肥明), N. Nishimura (西村信哉), M. Hashimoto (橋本正章), Y. Matsuo (松尾康秀), T. Noda (野田常雄), S. Nagataki (長瀧重博)
arxiv-2105-13958.description: Abstract Type I X-ray bursts are thermonuclear explosions on the neutron star (NS) surface caused by mass accretion from a companion star. Observations of X-ray bursts provide valuable information on X-ray binary systems, e.g., binary parameters, the chemical composition of accreted matter, and the nuclear equation of state (EOS) of NSs.

arxiv-2112-07689.title: Peculiar Hydrogen-deficient Carbon Stars: Strontium-Rich Stars and the s-Process
arxiv-2112-07689.creator: Courtney L. Crawford, Patrick Tisserand, Geoffrey C. Clayton, Bradley Munson
arxiv-2112-07689.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Courtney L. Crawford, Patrick Tisserand, Geoffrey C. Clayton, Bradley Munson. R Coronae Borealis (RCB) variables and their non-variable counterparts, the dustless Hydrogen-Deficient Carbon (dLHdC) stars have been known to exhibit enhanced s -processed material on their surfaces, especially Sr, Y, and Ba. No comprehensive work has been done to explore the s -process in these types of stars, however one particular RCB star, U Aqr, has been under scrutiny for its extraordinary Sr enhancement.

arxiv-2305-08196.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Segment Anything Model for Vision and Beyond
arxiv-2305-08196.creator: Chunhui Zhang, Li Liu, Yawen Cui, Guanjie Huang, Weilin Lin, Yiqian Yang, Yuehong Hu
arxiv-2305-08196.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chunhui Zhang, Li Liu, Yawen Cui, Guanjie Huang, Weilin Lin, Yiqian Yang, Yuehong Hu. Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving towards artificial general intelligence, which refers to the ability of an AI system to perform a wide range of tasks and exhibit a level of intelligence similar to that of a human being. This is in contrast to narrow or specialized AI, which is designed to perform specific tasks with a high degree of efficiency.

arxiv-2306-04814.title: Revisiting Inferential Benchmarks for Knowledge Graph Completion
arxiv-2306-04814.creator: Shuwen Liu, Bernardo Cuenca Grau, Ian Horrocks, Egor V. Kostylev
arxiv-2306-04814.description: Abstract Knowledge Graph (KG) completion is the problem of extending an incomplete KG with missing facts. A key feature of Machine Learning approaches for KG completion is their ability to learn inference patterns, so that the predicted facts are the results of applying these patterns to the KG.

arxiv-2407-06649.title: On the equivalence problem of Smith forms for multivariate polynomial matrices
arxiv-2407-06649.creator: Dong Lu, Dingkang Wang, Fanghui Xiao, Xiaopeng Zheng
arxiv-2407-06649.description: Abstract This paper delves into the equivalence problem of Smith forms for multivariate polynomial matrices. Generally speaking, multivariate ( n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 ) polynomial matrices and their Smith forms may not be equivalent. However, under certain specific condition, we derive the necessary and sufficient condition for their equivalence.

arxiv-2512-04895.title: Chameleon: Adaptive Adversarial Agents for Scaling-Based Visual Prompt Injection in Multimodal AI Systems Thanks:
arxiv-2512-04895.creator: M Zeeshan, Saud Satti
arxiv-2512-04895.description: Abstract Multimodal Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, particularly Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have become integral to critical applications ranging from autonomous decision-making to automated document processing. As these systems scale, they rely heavily on preprocessing pipelines to handle diverse inputs efficiently. However, this dependency on standard preprocessing operations, specifically image downscaling, creates a significant yet often overlooked security vulnerability.

pmc-10704072.title: Risks for Readmission Among Older Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: An Analysis Using Korean National Health Insurance Service – Senior Cohort Data
pmc-10704072.creator: Yu Seong Hwang, Heui Sug Jo
pmc-10704072.description: ObjectivesThe high readmission rate of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has led to the worldwide establishment of proactive measures for identifying and mitigating readmissions. This study aimed to identify factors associated with readmission, as well as groups particularly vulnerable to readmission that require transitional care services.

pmc-11354241.title: Genetic Variants in the TBC1D2B Gene Are Associated with Ramon Syndrome and Hereditary Gingival Fibromatosis
pmc-11354241.creator: Thatphicha Kularbkaew, Tipaporn Thongmak, Phan Sandeth, Teerada Daroontum, Callum S. Durward, Pichai Vittayakittipong, Paul Duke, Anak Iamaroon, Sompid Kintarak, Worrachet Intachai, Chumpol Ngamphiw, Sissades Tongsima, Peeranat Jatooratthawichot, Timothy C. Cox, James R. Ketudat Cairns, Piranit Kant
pmc-11354241.description: Ramon syndrome (MIM 266270) is an extremely rare genetic syndrome, characterized by gingival fibromatosis, cherubism-like lesions, epilepsy, intellectual disability, hypertrichosis, short stature, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, and ocular abnormalities. Hereditary or non-syndromic gingival fibromatosis (HGF) is also rare and considered to represent a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by benign, slowly progressive, non-inflammatory gingival overgrowth.

pmc-11606119.title: AKT kinases as therapeutic targets
pmc-11606119.creator: Dalal Hassan, Craig W Menges, Joseph R Testa, Alfonso Bellacosa
pmc-11606119.description: AKT, or protein kinase B, is a central node of the PI3K signaling pathway that is pivotal for a range of normal cellular physiologies that also underlie several pathological conditions, including inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, overgrowth syndromes, and neoplastic transformation.

pmc-12510132.title: Impact of Tendon Gap on Decision-Making in Acute Achilles Tendon Rupture: A Systematic Review
pmc-12510132.creator: Mohamed Elbeshbeshy, Mohamed Khalafallah, Adam Fell, Andrew Davies, Mohamed Hashem
pmc-12510132.description: Acute Achilles tendon rupture (AATR) is a prevalent injury that significantly impacts clinical decision-making, particularly concerning the initial gap size following the rupture. This review aims to evaluate the influence of initial gap size on treatment decisions in managing acute Achilles tendon complete ruptures.

pmc-12826787.title: Minimally invasive surgery in paediatric nephroblastoma
pmc-12826787.creator: Steven W Warmann, Jörg Fuchs
pmc-12826787.description: Surgery is a corner stone of treatment in children with nephroblastoma. Over recent years, the evolution of surgical guidelines has added to the improvement of treatment results in affected children. Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) has been described as part of this evolution. The present article summarises the current recommendations for MIS in nephroblastoma based on the relevant global treatment protocols.

pmc-13114821.title: Effects of Cricket Powder Supplementation on Gut Microbiota in High-Fat Diet-Fed Mice
pmc-13114821.creator: Yanjun Guo, Rui-Qi Shi, Ananya Dechakhamphu, Min Zhao, Ju-Sheng Zheng, Sirithon Siriamornpun
pmc-13114821.description: The gut microbiota plays an important role in host physiology and is highly influenced by dietary factors. This study aimed to investigate the effects of cricket powder (CP) supplementation on gut microbiota composition in high-fat diet-fed C57BL/6J mice. Male C57BL/6J mice were fed a normal diet or a high-fat diet.

pmc-13116773.title: Solution-Based Research to Address Disparities in Precision Cancer Health: A Case Report Elucidating the Design and Rationale of the Illinois Cancer Health Equity Research (I-CHER) Center
pmc-13116773.creator: Frank A. Granata, Aileen Shen, Karissa Cerda, Monet Jones, Osei Bekoe, Erica Seltzer, Julie Bobitt, Margaret Wright, Paola Torres, Carolina Bujanda, Angelina Izguerra, L. A. Naiche, Vivian Pan, Ana Waite, Keith Naylor, Patrick Smith, Ryan Nguyen, Leslie Carnahan, Vida Henderson, Kent Hoskins, Chinwe
pmc-13116773.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? The work conducted by the I-CHER Center directly addresses persistent, multi-faceted cancer health disparities and highlights the multilevel factors that drive them—including structural, social, and biological determinants—which result in a disproportionate burden of advanced-stage cancer diagnosis and worse outcomes for highly vulnerable populations.

pmc-13225536.title: Association between the development of sepsis and the BAR index in patients with acute pancreatitis: A retrospective investigation based on MIMIC-IV database
pmc-13225536.creator: Jinhai Wang, Fuhong Zheng, Lei Zhu, Haibo Liu
pmc-13225536.description: Sepsis, as a severe complication of acute pancreatitis (AP), needs to be identified and treated as early as possible. The blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio (BAR) index has shown good predictive ability in many studies. However, its effectiveness in predicting AP complicated by sepsis has not been further verified.

pmc-13669330.title: Epigenetic regulation of humoral immunity: molecular mechanisms, diseases and therapeutic targets
pmc-13669330.creator: Shaocun Zhang, Yu Wang, Xin Min, Yuzhang Wu, Wanli Liu
pmc-13669330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Humoral immunity, a fundamental branch of adaptive immunity, relies on B lymphocytes and the antibodies they produce to eliminate extracellular pathogens and neutralize toxins. The development, activation, and differentiation of B cells are tightly regulated by epigenetic mechanisms—including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin dynamics, RNA modifications, and noncoding RNAs—that modulate gene expression without altering the DNA sequence, orchestrating key events such as V(D)J recombination, class switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, germinal center reactions, and the generation of memory B cells and plasma cells.
